description.value: Stikine River Song Cafe & Lodge occupies the historic Hudson's Bay Trading Post in Telegraph Creek, one of BC's most remote communities deep in Tāłtān Territory, accessible via a long gravel road from Dease Lake. The café is celebrated locally and by travellers for hearty homemade meals and freshly baked pies, and doubles as the community gathering place. The same building holds nine renovated lodge rooms — some with kitchenettes — making it a rare full-service stop for cyclists undertaking wilderness expeditions in the upper Stikine River corridor.

address.value: 1 Stikine Avenue, Box 46, Telegraph Creek BC, Canada V0J 2W0

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website is fully accessible and provides strong evidence for a real, operating seasonal café and lodge in Telegraph Creek, BC. The /stay page explicitly mentions 'shared communal washrooms' and a guest review confirms 'Starlink wifi was very fast,' supporting washrooms=true and Wi-Fi=true. OSM has no phone or address to cross-check, but the website supplies both; the OSM name ('Stikine River Song') is a shortened form of the website's consistent branding ('Stikine River Song Cafe & Lodge'), which is flagged as a discrepancy.
concerns: OSM name 'Stikine River Song' is a truncated form of the website's consistent branding 'Stikine River Song Cafe & Lodge'; OSM name may benefit from updating.
OSM opening_hours tag appears to conflict with hours shown across all website pages; OSM data may be outdated.
Seasonal operation (May–September) noted on website; OSM has no seasonal qualifier — cyclists visiting off-season may find it closed.
OSM had no phone or address tags; both sourced entirely from website and not cross-checked against OSM.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Real, operating seasonal café and lodge with confirmed website, phone, and address — a genuine and notable stop for cyclists traversing one of BC's most remote routes.
enrichment_extras.notes: Located in Telegraph Creek, accessible via a long, unpaved road from Dease Lake. Website advises travellers to call ahead from Dease Lake on their day of travel to check road conditions — relevant safety information for touring cyclists. Operated under the Tāłtān Nation (contact email domain @tahltan.ca).
